A tutor that listens, not just one that marks.

Upload a photo of your work whenever you're ready. Your tutor looks at your actual piece, every time, and tells you honestly what's working and one clear thing to try next.

If it gets something wrong, you tell it, and it adjusts, just as a good teacher would.

Still life: egg studyAn example conversation
TutorLovely soft form on the shell. That bright highlight near the top feels a little sharp for such diffused light. Could you soften its edges?
YouThat's not a highlight. It's a tiny feather stuck to the egg.
TutorAh, that's a much better story! Let's make it read as a feather: a few fine, broken strokes with a drier brush, and a whisper of shadow underneath so it sits on the shell rather than glowing from it.

A few honest answers

Is the feedback genuinely personal, or just generic AI output?

Genuinely personal. The AI tutor looks at your actual photo, every time, not a script or a template. It tells you honestly when something's working and gives you one real thing to try next, specific to what you made. If a piece is already excellent, it says so, rather than inventing a fix nobody needs.

Is there a subscription?

No. Everything is a one-off payment: £5 for a side-shoot, £10 for a course, £60 for an Academy tier. Nothing renews automatically.

Can I try it before paying anything?

Yes. Your first side-shoot is completely free, with real feedback and no card required. See how it feels before deciding on anything.

I've genuinely never drawn before. Is this actually for me?

Yes, more than for anyone else. This exists for people who'd normally say "I can't draw" or "I'm just not creative." You're creating more than you realise already. This gives it structure, and someone paying proper attention.

Do I need to buy materials?

Use whatever you already have. If you'd like a matching set, each course links to a kit from our partner Artway. We may earn a small commission on kits bought through our links.

What happens to my images? Is my work still mine?

Completely yours, always. We never claim any rights over what you create. If you'd ever like a piece shown in our community gallery, that's entirely optional and your choice.

How is this different from something like Skillshare?

Platforms like Skillshare give you videos to watch, which is useful, but nobody ever looks at what you make. Here, every piece you submit gets individual feedback. That's the whole point.

Can I sell what I make?

Yes. Ulverston Art House also runs a seller marketplace. Once you've made something you're proud of, you can register as a vendor and sell it yourself on the same site.

Start where you're comfortable.

Try one side-shoot free and see how the feedback feels. There's no card needed and nothing to cancel.
